summary:
# Notes on the 5-book corpus (Gutenberg/public-domain novels)

Use these notes in place of the source text. Each BOOK is separate.

---

## BOOK 1 — *Just a Girl* (Charles Garvice, 1895; Gutenberg 57166)

**Setting:** Three Star Camp, Australian gold camp (Wally River valley). Dan MacGrath's Eldorado saloon; Varley Howard (gambler, tall silk hat, white hand, diamond scarf-pin, languid voice). Bill the postman (oldish, grizzled, huge mouth). Found a nameless infant (later Esmeralda) under a dead woman on the road near Dog's Ear; Varley won her by cards (high card, an ace); she was named Esmeralda Howard by the camp (suggested by the doctor). Mother Melinda (old woman, nurse, "Melinda" maternal). Taffy (Welshman, giant, "Wild Welshman"), The Penman (old schoolmaster), Sir/“Smifkens” baronet, the lawyer, the doctor (Parson). Esmeralda: auburn/red-gold hair, dark brown eyes, freckles, rides, shoots, swims the Wally, tracks; her pony/chestnut; Redfern habit.

**Plot, in order:**
1. Esmeralda grows up adored by the camp; cradle bought from Ballarat by Taffy; measles; learns reluctantly from The Penman. Varley tells her she must learn to read; she says she'll marry him; he refuses ("I am old enough to be your father").
2. Norman (Lord) Druce, young Englishman, lost, shot in leg at Dog's Ear; Esmeralda rescues him from an ambush, stops the bullet hit in her hat (hole in hat). Taffy names him "Pink Rosebud." Bullet extracted; Esmeralda keeps it. Norman sings in the Eldorado; proposes by moonlit river; she refuses.
3. Mr Samson Pinchook (solicitor, Pinchook, Pinchook & Becham, 119 Grey's Inn) arrives: grandfather Gordon Chetwynde, millionaire (over two million pounds); her father Chetwynde, mother died; Varley introduces her as Miss Chetwynde. Her aunt/guardian: Lady Wyndover (Grosvenor Square; Mount Street; Deepdale in Surrey). Esmeralda leaves camp amid farewell (concertina plays "Auld Lang Syne"; Taffy's note; Norman's note: "I can not stay here now that there is no hope for me...").
4. In London: Lady Wyndover, Madame Cerise (dressmaker), Barker (maid). Esmeralda meets Lord Trafford (Marquis of Trafford, eldest son of Duke of Belfayre; cousin of Norman) at Lady Blankyre's; Lady Ada Lancing (fair, cold, loves Trafford, poor Scotch peer's daughter). Lord Selvaine (Trafford's uncle, "master-mind", small, grey) plots marriage with rich heiress to save Belfayre (mortgaged; "Messrs. Levy, Moses and Aaron"). Trafford proposes at Shirley/West Wickham drive. Lilias Selvaine (niece of Duke, small, dark, 19, mistress of Belfayre). Duke of Belfayre (old, white-haired, kind; loves Esmeralda; calls her "my dear"). Duke's watering-place scheme; Mr Helby the steward; Ada's threat ("you will be miserable").
5. Esmeralda overhears Ada and Trafford in anteroom at wedding eve/after; learns marriage was for money. Wedding ceremony at church; breakfast; Norman present; Ada bridesmaid; Lilias; Ada steals Norman's letter (from Dal; "I can not stay here..."). Esmeralda leaves Belfayre by night; visits duke's bedside, kisses him, a tear falls; duke dies (Esmeralda the Duchess). Esmeralda flees to Three Star, adopted back by Varley, Mother Melinda, the boys.
6. Trafford follows to Australia, meets Varley at Raven Claim; Varley's duel challenge (Simon as umpire; Esmeralda interposes; Varley's shot wounds her shoulder). Reconciliation; Norman confesses; Ada revealed as author of deceit (letter theft, telegram). Trafford and Esmeralda reconcile at Three Star; married happily. Norman and Lilias marry. Varley visits England; Lady Ada on Continent.

Key quotes: "Esmeralda! Esmeralda! And luck to her!"; Varley: "Boys, Esmeralda's come back! ... She's come back and she's come to stay!"; "I love but thee" is in BOOK 2 not here.

## BOOK 2 — *Only One Love, or Who Was the Heir* (Charles Garvice; Gutenberg 35523)

**Characters:** Jack Newcombe ("the Savage", 22, Oxford, spendthrift, honest); Redmond/“Squire” Ralph Davenant (dying; Hurst Leigh); Stephen Davenant (nephew, smooth, pale, "Fascination Davenant", hypocrite, forges/steals will); Gideon Rolfe (woodman, Warden Forest, Una's supposed father; formerly Hurst schoolmaster's son, loved Caroline Hatfield, who was Ralph's secret wife); Una (Eunice Davenant, daughter of Ralph & Caroline, 21, dark-brown eyes, bright brown hair, dog-rose kiss); Martha Rolfe (Gideon's wife); Bersak? (no—Dick the deerhound in Book 2 is Gideon's dog); Mrs. Davenant (Stephen's mother, timid, Walmington Square); Laura Treherne (Stephen's pledged fiancée, dark eyes, "Remember!"; later as "Mary Burns" maid to Lady Bell); Janet? (no). Lady Isabel "Lady Bell" Earlsley (heiress, colonial, witty, loves Jack); Mrs Fellowes (companion); Leonard Dagle (Jack's barrister friend, Spider Court, Temple; loves Laura); Felix Hoffman (racecourse sharp); Mrs Hoffman; Janet Todd (Eli's daughter, eloped with Warren Courtly); Eli Todd (stud groom); Skettle (Hudsley's clerk, parish-clerk type); James Hudsley (lawyer); Slummers (Stephen's valet, shadow); Dr Harding; Sir Humphrey (physician); Moss (money-lender, Levy Moss); Sir Arkroyd Hetley; Lord Dalrymple ("Dally"); Lord Pierrepoint.

**Plot, in order:**
1. Jack lost in Warden Forest; cider and cake; quarrel with Gideon; Una's face; Gideon forbids. Jack meets Una by the lake; a stranger deserves no kiss; he kisses her hand; Gideon attacks him with stick.
2. Ralph Davenant dies, night after the quarrel anniversary; Stephen steals the "last will" (July 18) and destroys? No—Stephen keeps it, reads: fortune to Una, £50,000 to Jack, sermons to Stephen. Stephen hides the will; Jack finds a torn/scorched bit, Skettle keeps it.
3. Stephen takes Mrs Davenant to Warden; persuades Gideon to surrender Una; Una moves to Walmington Square under Mrs Davenant. Jack and Una meet in London (Lady Bell's ball/picnic at Richmond). Jack repeatedly courts Una; Lady Bell's crush on Jack; Jack's debts to Moss; Jack's dream of marrying Una; Stephen pretends help, offers Jack a government post. Stephen plots to win Una himself.
4. Gideon, Stephen confront; Stephen tells Jack that Una is illegitimate and Gideon's child—Jack writes a renouncing letter ("Forget me, Una"); Stephen keeps it. Una collapses at tea. Stephen takes Una to Clumley to marry; she is rescued at Netherton inn by Gideon, Jack and Laura Treherne; Stephen flees; Skettle produces will fragment; Jack and Una reconciled; Lady Bell helps Laura. Final chapter: Jack and Una married at Hurst; Gideon attends; Stephen becomes philanthropist and is pitied; Lady Bell and Laura Treherne (with Leonard) attend.

Quote: "Yes, dear, I love but thee."

## BOOK 3 — *Won at Last; or, Mrs. Briscoe's Nephews* (Agnes Giberne)

**Characters:** Marion Hazel (narrator, mother of nine: Jack eldest, Cherry and Cresswell/Cress twins, Owen, Fred, Robert, Edmund, Ted youngest; "Bob" and "Teddie"); Robert Hazel (husband, City clerk, careworn, kindly; mother-in-law no); Mrs Elizabeth Briscoe (Aunt Briscoe, widow at "The Gables", sharp-tongued, rheumatic; husband Uncle Briscoe); Churton Hazel (Robert's younger brother, selfish, loud, went to Canada/US); Maimie (Mary) Browne, Churton's stepdaughter, 14, flaxen curls, black eyes, pretty, independent; her mother (Mrs Browne, dead); Mr Wilson (lawyer); Maria (Aunt Briscoe's maid); cook.

**Plot, in order:**
1. Robert and Marion's cheap life; Cherry sews; Cress wants shoes/jacket; Jack slow at school and office. Aunt Briscoe's Thursday letter invites Robert and a child. Maimie arrives with Churton's letters; claims cousinhood; letters examined; Churton has not written; Maimie insists she is not an impostor. Maimie stays, helps with work, teaches boys; clashes with Marion; Maimie's illness (inflammation, measles); Jack's devotion; Maimie teaches Jack arithmetic.
2. Aunt Briscoe's £5 gift; Churton's £25 bank-note; Cress leaves for India job; Jack and Maimie; Cress's jealousy; Cress strikes Jack, Maimie's arm bruised.
3. Churton returns; Maimie's confrontation: demands he repay expenses or take her; Churton sends her to Aunt Briscoe's (Churton is there, had changed Aunt Briscoe's will, leaving everything to himself). Maimie discovers and rectifies; lawyer Wilson; will reads: codicil three weeks back leaves all to Churton; later codicil restores to Robert, £1000 to Jack. Churton storms out, disowns Maimie; she goes to Robert and Marion.
4. Jack and Maimie marry three years later at Robert's home; "The Gables" to Jack and Maimie's cottage.

Key phrase: "Won at last"—Jack wins Maimie.

## BOOK 4 — *The Runaways* (Nat Gould, 1900s; Gutenberg 39631)

**Characters:** Redmond Maynard (Squire of Hazelwell, Rushshire; dog Bersak, wolfhound; mare Honeysuckle, horse Random); Ulick Maynard (his son; left home two years earlier after accusation re Janet; now owns racehorse the Saint, grey by Father Confessor out of Hilda, racing as "Mr Lanark"); Irene Carstone (ward, later Mrs Courtly, then Mrs Maynard; painter); Warren Courtly (husband of Irene, Anselm Manor, gambler, secret affair with Janet; dies in Glen church leap); Eli Todd (stud manager, ex-hussar; daughter Janet Todd eloped with Warren); Mary Marley (Mrs Courtly's maid, later married Bob Heather); Bob Heather (groom); Martha Dixon (housekeeper at Anselm); Dr Harding (doctor); James Bard (vet, Helton); Sam Lane (huntsman); Fred May (trainer at Epsom); Ben Sprig (jockey); Felix Hoffman (sharp, blackmailer; mother Mrs Hoffman at Feltham); Aaron Hyam (bookmaker, Gum Tree Hotel? that's Book 5).

**Plot, in order:**
1. Snowy New Year's Eve two years after Ulick's departure; Squire waits up; Irene stays at Hazelwell. Honeysuckle's colt foals; Ulick secretly visits Eli; Ulick learns Janet left the same night.
2. Ulick buys the Saint (£200 guineas) from Fred May's find; wins Kempton Pastures Handicap (ridden by Ben Sprig); Warren's jealousy of Random.
3. Irene's painting of Random; Felix Hoffman's blackmail letters; Warren's Holme Farm sale for £10,000. Janet discovered; Irene's visit to Feltham.
4. Reconciliation of Squire and Ulick at Newmarket/Walton Hotel; Coronation Cup at Epsom: the Saint beats Vulture by a short head.
5. Hunt at Helton/Brecon Wood: Ulick rides Random; Warren challenges, jumps Glen church wall, dies.
6. Ulick and Irene marry; child; Janet returns to Eli.

---

## BOOK 5 — *Settling Day* (Nat Gould; Gutenberg 35496)

**Characters:** Jim Dennis (owner of Wanabeen station, New South Wales; wronged man; wife Maud deserted him and child); Willie Dennis (son, 6 then 12; jockey, yellow jacket); Sal (half-caste woman, former mission girl, housekeeper, devoted to Willie; "King Charlie" tribal chief); Dr Tom Sheridan (drunken, kind doctor at Swamp Creek; dog Baalim; violin; poet); Ned Glenn (coach driver); Constable Doonan (police; later sergeant); Sergeant Machinson (corrupt); Adye Dauntsey (police magistrate, Barragong); Abe Dalton (outlaw, Barker's Creek gang); Seth Sharp (murderer); Rodney Shaw (Cudgegong station owner, villain; stole Maud; attacks Sal); Benjamin Nix (manager); Silas Dixon (hand); Alec Beg; Neptune (grey stallion by Seahorse out of Mermaid); Grey Bird (four-year-old grey, Neptune's son, out of Seamew); Distant Shore; The Captain; Jack Ashton (jockey, Defiance); Molly Corbold (later Mrs Jim Dennis); Chris Shaw (cousin, buys Cudgegong).

**Plot, in order:**
1. Willie, aged six, nearly dies; Jim rides for Dr Tom; Sal nurses. Sal's backstory (her mother/black fellow; King Charlie's curse).
2. Maud's desertion; Jim's bitter loss; Ned Glenn; Jim tames horses; Rodney Shaw returns from England; stolen stallion Seahorse found on Wanabeen; Jim returns him; Shaw's hostility.
3. Dr Tom saves Abe Dalton's life on condition Dalton's gang leave Dennis alone.
4. Swamp Creek races: Willie rides Neptune (yellow jacket), beats Distant Shore by a short head; Willie struck on head the night before (by Dalton).
5. Shaw's abduction of Sal; Sal escapes via white-ant-eaten floor; King Charlie's tribe; the attack on Barker's Creek; Dalton shot by Sergeant Machinson's assailant? (Dalton shoots Machinson; Dauntsey wounds Dalton); Rodney Shaw wounded at Barker's Creek, dies at Cudgegong after Jim's confrontation.
6. Maud returns to die at Wanabeen; Willie not told she is his mother; she dies; Jim forgives her.
7. Sydney Cup: Grey Bird wins by a neck over Bung Bung, despite broken stirrup leather; Jim to buy Cudgegong from Chris Shaw.
8. Later: Molly Corbold marries Jim; Dr Tom prosperous; Sal married Doonan; Jim contented.
